## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 12 (*Dubbaca*, "Being difficult to correct") is the twelfth rule in the *Saṅghādisesa* section of the Theravāda *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga*. The rule stipulates that a monk who refuses admonition regarding monastic transgressions and proves obstinate is subject to formal suspension. Its origin story features the monk Channa, who was notoriously proud and intractable when corrected by his fellow monastics. Modern English translation is provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 A corresponding nun's rule is preserved as Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 16 and in non-Theravāda Bhikṣuṇī Vibhaṅgas.
